structure.overview: The Applicant seeks judicial review of the Immigration Appeal Division's (IAD) decision excluding her from permanent residence under paragraph 117(9)(d) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR) due to non-declaration as a dependent. The IAD found it lacked jurisdiction to consider humanitarian and compassionate grounds since the Applicant was not a family class member. The Federal Court dismissed the application, finding the IAD's decision reasonable and consistent with the law.

party_points.text: IAD failed to consider evidence and made contradictory determinations
Appeal submitted DNA test, financial support proof, affidavit, photos to establish relationship
Acknowledged citation errors in reply submissions without explanation

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The Applicant seeks judicial review of the IAD decision, alleging failure to consider evidence and contradictory determinations; the Respondent defends the decision.

citations.cite: subsection 72(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, SC 2001, c 27 [IRPA]
citations.why: Applicant relies on judicial review provision

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court dismisses the application for judicial review.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: An immigration officer refused the Applicant's PR application, finding she was not a dependent child or declared family member, and excluded under paragraph 117(9)(d) IRPR.

citations.cite: section 2 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, SOR/2002-227 [IRPR]

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Mr. Adeleke appealed, submitting evidence including DNA test, financial support proof, affidavit, and photos to establish relationship with Applicant.
idea_list: Mr. Adeleke's appeal and evidence submission

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The IAD accepted Mr. Adeleke's explanation for non-declaration but found he still failed to declare the Applicant as a non-accompanying dependent, excluding her under paragraph 117(9)(d).
idea_list: IAD found Applicant excluded under paragraph 117(9)(d)

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The IAD found it lacked jurisdiction to assess humanitarian and compassionate considerations since Applicant was not family class member, but noted other PR application options.
idea_list: IAD lacks jurisdiction for H&C assessment

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court explains the reasonableness standard from Vavilov and Mason, placing burden on challenger to show serious shortcomings.
idea_list: Reasonableness standard and burden of proof

citations.cite: Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65 at para 85 [Vavilov]
Mason v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2023 SCC 21 at para 8 [Mason]

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court finds the Applicant's arguments unpersuasive.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court explains section 117 of IRPR, especially paragraph 117(9)(d), which excludes certain non-accompanying family members from family class.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court notes it is undisputed Mr. Adeleke failed to declare the Applicant, and paragraph 117(9)(d) is a strict provision excluding non-disclosed family members.

citations.cite: Nguyen v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2010 FC 133 at para 55 [Nguyen]
Adjani v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2008 FC 32 at para 32

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The IAD acknowledged evidence including DNA test but found section 117(9)(d) requires all non-accompanying dependents be included without exception.
idea_list: IAD acknowledged evidence but applied strict rule

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The IAD reasonably found Applicant excluded under paragraph 117(9)(d); family reunification and lack of fraud do not alter this legal provision.
idea_list: IAD's exclusion finding reasonable despite family reunification objective

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The IAD correctly found it lacked jurisdiction to consider H&C factors under section 65 IRPA in sponsorship appeals when Applicant is not family class.
idea_list: IAD lacks jurisdiction for H&C in this context

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Public Policy exemption does not apply as Mr. Adeleke became PR under economic class, and the issue was not challenged before the IAD.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Applicant has not shown the IAD's decision is unreasonable.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Respondent's counsel noted Applicant's reply submissions contained mismatched and inaccurate authorities.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Applicant's counsel acknowledged citation errors but did not explain their cause; court notes errors resemble AI-generated mistakes.
idea_list: Applicant acknowledges citation errors; court notes AI-like errors

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Court cannot conclude errors arose from undeclared AI use but reminds counsel to disclose AI use per Notice and warns of sanctions for non-compliance.

citations.cite: Notice to the Parties and the Profession on the Use of Artificial Intelligence in Court Proceedings, dated May 7, 2024
Hussein v Canada (Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship), 2025 FC 1138 at paras 9–14, 16
citations.why: Sanctions for failure to disclose AI use

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: No serious question of general importance for certification is proposed or found by the court.
